coverage: All 26 sections, both English editions: named writers, artists, performers, critics, cited story figures and the grammatical example Cleon. Work titles without an identified person are not turned into people.

entities.name: Homer
entities.body: The ancient Greek poet traditionally credited with the Iliad and Odyssey.

entities.name: Empedocles
entities.body: The Greek philosopher who wrote about nature in verse.

entities.name: Sophron
entities.body: The writer of mimes whom Aristotle pairs with Xenarchus.

entities.name: Xenarchus
entities.body: The writer of mimes whom Aristotle pairs with Sophron.

entities.name: Chaeremon
entities.body: The poet whose Centaur combines different metres.

entities.name: Polygnotus
entities.body: The Greek painter Aristotle cites for noble portrayals of people.

entities.name: Pauson
entities.body: The painter Aristotle contrasts with Polygnotus.

entities.name: Dionysius
entities.body: The painter cited for portraying people as they are.

entities.name: Cleophon
entities.body: The poet cited for ordinary subjects and plain diction.

entities.name: Hegemon
entities.body: The Thasian poet whom Aristotle credits with inventing parodies.

entities.name: Nicochares
entities.body: The poet named as the author of the Deiliad.

entities.name: Timotheus
entities.body: The poet and musician whose treatment of the Cyclops is compared with Philoxenus’s.

entities.name: Philoxenus
entities.body: The poet and musician whose treatment of the Cyclops is compared with Timotheus’s.

entities.name: Sophocles
entities.body: The Athenian tragic playwright, author of Oedipus and Antigone.

entities.name: Aristophanes
entities.body: The Athenian comic playwright.

entities.name: Epicharmus
entities.body: The early comic poet associated here with Sicily.

entities.name: Chionides
entities.body: An early comic poet mentioned alongside Magnes.

entities.name: Magnes
entities.body: An early comic poet mentioned alongside Chionides.

entities.name: Aeschylus
entities.body: The Athenian tragic playwright, credited here with increasing the number of actors.

entities.name: Crates
entities.body: The Athenian comic playwright credited with moving beyond personal lampoon.

entities.name: Euripides
entities.body: The Athenian tragic playwright, author of Medea and other plays discussed here.

entities.name: Zeuxis
entities.body: The Greek painter used as a point of comparison for dramatic characterization.

entities.name: Herodotus
entities.body: The Greek historian whose writing is contrasted with poetry.

entities.name: Alcibiades
entities.body: The Athenian public figure cited as a named subject of lampoon.

entities.name: Agathon
entities.body: The tragic playwright whose work supplies several examples in the discussion.

entities.name: Mitys
entities.body: The man of Argos commemorated by the statue in Aristotle’s example of striking coincidence.

entities.name: Astydamas
entities.body: The tragic playwright named as the author of an Alcmaeon.

entities.name: Carcinus
entities.body: The tragic playwright whose plays supply examples of recognition and staging.

entities.name: Polyidus
entities.body: The sophist whose handling of the Iphigenia story Aristotle discusses.

entities.name: Theodectes
entities.body: The tragic playwright whose Tydeus and Lynceus are discussed.

entities.name: Dicaeogenes
entities.body: The playwright named as the author of the Cyprians.

entities.name: Protagoras
entities.body: The Greek sophist whose criticism of Homer’s opening invocation is discussed.

entities.name: Sthenelus
entities.body: The poet whose diction is cited alongside Cleophon’s.

entities.name: Eucleides
entities.body: The critic called Eucleides the elder, who mocked poets’ manipulation of syllables.

entities.name: Ariphrades
entities.body: The critic who ridiculed the unusual phrasing of tragic poets.

entities.name: Xenophanes
entities.body: The Greek poet and thinker associated with criticism of stories about the gods.

entities.name: Hippias of Thasos
entities.body: The interpreter cited for resolving passages through accent or breathing.

entities.name: Glaucon
entities.body: The critic cited on readers who blame poets on the basis of their own assumptions.

entities.name: Mynniscus
entities.body: The older actor who criticized Callippides’s extravagant gestures.

entities.name: Callippides
entities.body: The actor criticized for exaggerated movement.

entities.name: Pindarus
entities.body: The performer mentioned in the discussion of excessive acting.

entities.name: Sosistratus
entities.body: The epic reciter criticized for overdone gesticulation.

entities.name: Mnasitheus
entities.body: The performer from Opus cited for excessive gesture in lyrical competition.

entities.name: Margites
entities.body: The foolish hero whose name titles the comic poem attributed here to Homer.

entities.name: Heracles
entities.body: The Greek hero whose many exploits illustrate Aristotle’s point about unity of action.

entities.name: Odysseus
entities.body: The Greek hero of the Odyssey, husband of Penelope and father of Telemachus.

entities.name: Oedipus
entities.body: The legendary king of Thebes, central to the tragedy Aristotle repeatedly discusses.

entities.name: Orestes
entities.body: The son of Agamemnon, brother of Iphigenia and Electra, appearing in several dramatic examples.

entities.name: Iphigenia
entities.body: Agamemnon’s daughter and Orestes’s sister, the subject of several plays discussed here.

entities.name: Lynceus
entities.body: The Greek legendary figure whose story appears in Theodectes’s tragedy.

entities.name: Danaus
entities.body: The legendary king associated with the story of Lynceus.

entities.name: Thyestes
entities.body: The member of the royal house of Atreus whose story is a subject of tragedy.

entities.name: Alcmaeon
entities.body: The son of Eriphyle whose family story appears in tragic poetry.

entities.name: Meleager
entities.body: The Greek hero named among the families and figures used in tragedy.

entities.name: Telephus
entities.body: The legendary king of Mysia and a subject of tragedy.

entities.name: Aegisthus
entities.body: Clytemnestra’s partner and a figure in the story of Orestes.

entities.name: Clytemnestra
entities.body: The wife of Agamemnon and mother of Orestes.

entities.name: Eriphyle
entities.body: The mother of Alcmaeon in the tragic family story.

entities.name: Medea
entities.body: The woman from Colchis, wife of Jason, whose story Euripides dramatized.

entities.name: Telegonus
entities.body: Odysseus’s son in the story dramatized in the Wounded Odysseus.

entities.name: Antigone
entities.body: Oedipus’s daughter, the title figure of Sophocles’s play.

entities.name: Haemon
entities.body: Creon’s son and Antigone’s betrothed in Sophocles’s play.

entities.name: Creon
entities.body: The ruler of Thebes and father of Haemon in the Antigone example.

entities.name: Cresphontes
entities.body: The son of Merope in the recognition scene discussed here.

entities.name: Merope
entities.body: The mother in the recognition scene from Cresphontes.

entities.name: Helle
entities.body: The mythological figure whose name titles a play cited for a recognition scene.

entities.name: Menelaus
entities.body: The Spartan king and husband of Helen, appearing in a dramatic example.

entities.name: Scylla
entities.body: The mythological figure named in the Scylla example from a dithyramb.

entities.name: Melanippe
entities.body: The title figure of the tragedy cited for an inappropriately learned speech.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: The Greek warrior of the Trojan War, son of Peleus.

entities.name: Tyro
entities.body: The woman of Greek legend whose story supplies a recognition example.

entities.name: Tereus
entities.body: The legendary Thracian king whose story is dramatized in a play cited here.

entities.name: Alcinous
entities.body: The Phaeacian king who hosts Odysseus in the Odyssey.

entities.name: Tydeus
entities.body: The Greek hero whose name titles a play by Theodectes.

entities.name: The sons of Phineus
entities.body: The legendary family named by the title Phineidae.

entities.name: Amphiaraus
entities.body: The legendary seer whose story is used in an example about staging.

entities.name: Ajax
entities.body: The Greek warrior whose story provides an example of tragic suffering.

entities.name: Ixion
entities.body: The figure of Greek legend whose story is cited as a tragic subject.

entities.name: Peleus
entities.body: Achilles’s father, a legendary king and subject of drama.

entities.name: Prometheus
entities.body: The Titan whose story is used in Greek tragedy.

entities.name: Niobe
entities.body: The mother of Greek legend whose story appears in tragic poetry.

entities.name: Sisyphus
entities.body: The figure of Greek legend referred to in the discussion of drama.

entities.name: Philoctetes
entities.body: The Greek archer whose story is the subject of tragedies discussed here.

entities.name: Neoptolemus
entities.body: The son of Achilles who takes part in the Trojan War.

entities.name: Eurypylus
entities.body: The warrior named among the subjects drawn from the Little Iliad.

entities.name: Hector
entities.body: The Trojan warrior and opponent of Achilles in the Iliad.

entities.name: Laius
entities.body: The earlier king of Thebes in the story of Oedipus.

entities.name: Electra
entities.body: Agamemnon’s daughter and Orestes’s sister, a subject of tragedy.

entities.name: Dolon
entities.body: The Trojan scout discussed in an example from Homer.

entities.name: Ganymede
entities.body: The youth of Greek myth who serves as cupbearer to the gods.

entities.name: Icarius
entities.body: Penelope’s father in the question Aristotle discusses about Telemachus’s journey.

entities.name: Icadius
entities.body: The name given to Odysseus’s father-in-law in the alternative Cephallenian account Aristotle reports.

entities.name: Telemachus
entities.body: The son of Odysseus and Penelope.

entities.name: Aegeus
entities.body: The king of Athens whose appearance in Medea Aristotle discusses.

entities.name: Ares
entities.body: The Greek god of war.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: The chief god of the Greek pantheon.

entities.name: Dionysus
entities.body: The Greek god associated with wine and theatre.

entities.name: Poseidon
entities.body: The Greek sea god, an opponent of Odysseus in the Odyssey.

entities.name: Cleon, the son
entities.body: The son in the grammatical example “Cleon son of Cleon”; no historical person is identified.

entities.name: Cleon, the father
entities.body: The father in the grammatical example “Cleon son of Cleon”; no historical person is identified.

entities.name: Theodorus, the example name
entities.body: The personal name used to illustrate the parts of a compound word; no particular historical person is identified.

entities.name: Hermo-caico-xanthus
entities.body: The compound personal name used as a linguistic example.

entities.name: The Cyclops
entities.body: The one-eyed giant whose different portrayals by Timotheus and Philoxenus are compared.

entities.name: The daughters of Phorcys
entities.body: The mythical sisters named by the play title Phorcides.

entities.name: The women of Phthia
entities.body: The women named by the play title Phthiotides.
